questions.question: Define a superpower and explain why the United States and the Soviet Union were superpowers after 1945.
questions.expected_answer: A superpower has dominant global power: military strength and global reach (including nuclear weapons), economic strength, political and ideological leadership of an alliance and worldwide influence. The US was untouched at home, produced about half the world's manufactured goods, held most gold, had the largest navy and air force and the atomic bomb, and led new institutions. The USSR had the largest army, occupied Eastern Europe, led world communism, covered a vast territory, tested an atomic bomb in 1949 and led in space from 1957, though its economy was smaller.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the term Cold War and why it remained cold between the superpowers.
questions.expected_answer: The Cold War (about 1947-1991) was political, ideological, economic and military rivalry between the US-led West and the Soviet-led East without direct full-scale war between the superpowers. Orwell used the phrase in 1945; Baruch (1947) and Lippmann popularised it. It stayed cold mainly because of nuclear weapons and mutually assured destruction (MAD): second-strike capability meant any attacker would also be destroyed, deterring direct war, though crises like Cuba (1962) came close. The world was bipolar.

questions.question: Describe the methods used in the Cold War and explain how it affected Africa and South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Methods: alliances (NATO 1949; Warsaw Pact 1955), propaganda (Radio Free Europe; McCarthyism), espionage (CIA 1947, KGB 1954; U-2 incident 1960), arms and space races, aid, and proxy wars (Korea 1950-53, Vietnam, Afghanistan 1979-89, Angola). Africa: Congo crisis and Lumumba's murder (1961), support for Mobutu; Angola civil war from 1975 with USSR/Cuba versus US/South Africa. Apartheid government used anti-communism (Suppression of Communism Act 1950, total onslaught), fought the Border War (1966-89, Cuito Cuanavale 1987-88); ANC got Soviet support; Non-Aligned Movement (1961).
